fields.v: GPT-5.3-Codex best (61.8%), then Claude Opus 4.6 (57.6%), GPT-5.2 and Opus 4.6 Thinking (53.5%), Sonnet 4.6 (51.5%); open-weight models 5.1-23.4% (GLM-5 23.4%, Kimi-K2.5 17.5%, Qwen3.5 Plus 15.7%, MiniMax M2.5 14.9%, DeepSeek V3.2 5.1%; authors: GLM-5, Qwen 3.5 and Kimi K2.5 'hover around 15% to 24%'); lowest Grok 4.1 Fast Reasoning (1.2%). Gap MiniMax M2.5 vs Opus 4.6: 2.8% on SWE-Bench vs 42.7% on VCB. Higher cost and latency associated with higher accuracy with diminishing returns; Opus 4.6 near-top accuracy at lower cost and latency than GPT-5.3-Codex. Browser calls per app correlate with accuracy (r=0.72). All-model average falls from 34.18% (no integration) to 13.49% (email + Stripe), and from 44.29% (easy) to 21.36% (medium) to 6.03% (hard). Top-5 models: 12.8% of apps score zero vs 73.2% for bottom-5; 14.0% of bottom-5 apps fail to start. Only SE reported, no significance tests; authors say near-tie differences require caution
fields.quote: Open-weight models such as GLM 5, Qwen 3.5, and Kimi K2.5 hover around 15% to 24%, performing worse than leading closed-weight counterparts.
fields.where: §4.1 Overall Benchmark Performance, p. 5; Table 4, p. 6
fields.why: Table 4 marks five models as open-weight, including MiniMax M2.5 (14.85%) and DeepSeek V3.2 Thinking (5.11%), so the open-weight range is 5.1-23.4%, not 15-24%.
fields.doubt: A frase '15-24%' é dos autores só para GLM-5, Qwen e Kimi. Na Tabela 4 (pág. 6) há cinco modelos abertos (✓), incluindo MiniMax M2.5 (14,85%) e DeepSeek V3.2 (5,11%). Decide se o intervalo deve ser 5,1-23,4%.
